note: Reviewed per-tool policy for the HOL-Guard MCP server contribution of duckdb-vectors (hashgraph-online/hol-guard PR #6481). Staging reference captured in this repository; the canonical profile is contributions/mcp-servers/mcp.duckdb-vectors.json in the HOL-Guard PR. States: allow | review | block | inherit. Classification corrected after maintainer review: the server is NOT read-only (VectorStore connects writable and runs CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS on open), and search embeds via the configured backend (local by default; a network call under the opt-in Bedrock backend). MCP annotations are absent, so classification is justified from the server source.

tools.name: search
tools.rationale: Hybrid semantic + exact-token retrieval. Not auto-allowed: (1) opening the VectorStore connects writable and runs CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, so a call can create the database file and initialize schema/indexes (local-file-write); (2) it embeds the query via the configured backend, which is local by default but sends the query text over the network under the opt-in Bedrock backend (external-network-read); (3) it returns the indexed chunk text and metadata, not just match IDs, so an auto-allowed call would disclose corpus contents to the agent. review keeps coverage while leaving these to a local policy decision.

tools.name: report
tools.rationale: Index introspection (db_path, backend, dimensions, chunk count, sources). Not auto-allowed: opening the VectorStore connects writable and ensures schema, so even report can create the database file and its indexes on a missing/empty path (local-file-write); it also returns the database path and the indexed source paths, disclosing file layout. No network or embedding on this path. review rather than allow given the write-on-open behavior.

notExposedOverMcp: Explicit indexing (including the `mcp --index <folder>` startup build), deletes, and embedding/model configuration are CLI/SDK-level, not MCP tools. The startup index runs once in run_stdio before serving and is not a callable tool.
